gallery.description:
Australian Army soldiers with 8/12 Regiment, fire a M-777 Howitzer in support of U.S. Marines on the ground August 11, 2016 at Bradshaw Field Training Area, Northern Territory, Australia. The soldiers and Marines are taking part in Exercise Koolendong 16, a trilateral exercise between the Australian Defence Force, U.S. Marine Corps and French Armed Forces New Caledonia. 

(U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Sarah Anderson)

gallery.title: File:150716-N-NI474-263 (19912299375).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: A CH-53E Super Stallion, assigned to 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit, lifts a high mobility multi-purpose wheeled vehicle (HMMWV) after a regimental helo assault as part of Talisman Sabre 2015 at Bradshaw Field Training Area, Australia, July 16, 2015. Talisman Sabre is a biennial exercise that provides an invaluable opportunity for nearly 30,000 U.S. and Australian defense forces to conduct operations in a combined, joint and interagency environment that will increase both countries’ ability to plan and execute a full range of operations from combat missions to humanitarian assistance efforts. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Daniel M. Young/Released)

gallery.title: File:140822-M-PU373-163 (15027965381).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: From right, Australian army Artillery Lance Bombadier Aaron Costas, U.S. Marine Corps Capt. Aaron Brusch and U.S. Marine Corps 1st Lt. Sean M. Swallen work together to radio in a 10-digit grid Aug. 22, 2014, during a simulated company-sized attack as part of Koolendong 2014 at the Bradshaw Field Training Area in Northern Territory, Australia. The Marines were with the 1st Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, Marine Rotational Force-Darwin. The attack marked the beginning of the culminating event of Koolendong, an amphibious and live-fire exercise designed to increase interoperability between the U.S. Marine Corps and Australian Defense Force. (DoD photo by Lance Cpl. Joey S. Holeman Jr., U.S. Marine Corps/Released)
